questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

-89, -176, ?, -698, -1394, -2786, -5570
questions.solution:
Each term is double the previous one plus 2: −89 × 2 + 2 = −176, −176 × 2 + 2 = −350, −350 × 2 + 2 = −698, and so on. The missing term is −350.

**Answer: -350**

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

EA, GY, IW, ?, MS, OQ, QO, SM
questions.solution:
First letters advance +2 (E, G, I, K, M, O, Q, S) and second letters retreat −2 (A, Y, W, U, S, Q, O, M), so the missing cluster is KU.

**Answer: KU**

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

HJ : FD :: AC : YW :: EX : ?
questions.solution:
Each cluster shifts −2 on the first letter and −6 on the second (H→F, J→D; A→Y, C→W), so EX → CR.

**Answer: CR**

questions.q:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(MB, OF, RK) (DL, FP, IU)
questions.solution:
Within each trio the first letter moves +2 then +3 and the second +4 then +5; (MF, OJ, RO) fits: M+2 = O, F+4 = J; O+3 = R, J+5 = O.

**Answer: (MF, OJ, RO)**

questions.q: What will be the sum of number of days in the month of January, February, March and April in the year 2100?
questions.solution:
2100 is not a leap year (divisible by 100 but not by 400), so February has 28 days: 31 + 28 + 31 + 30 = 120 days.

**Answer: 120**

questions.q: What was the first day of the year 1906?
questions.solution:
Counting shifts from 1 Jan 1900 (Monday): six years pass with only 1904 a leap year, adding 6 + 1 = 7 days, so 1 Jan 1906 was also a Monday.

**Answer: Monday**

questions.q: Speed of 5 cars J, K, L, M and N is compared. Speed of no two cars is same. Speed of J is more than K. Speed of K is second lowest. Speed of L is less than N but more than M. Speed of J is less than only one car. Speed of which of the following car is more than J?
questions.solution:
J is faster than K but slower than exactly one car, so J is second fastest; L sits between N and M, and K is second slowest, giving N > J > L > K > M. Only N is faster than J.

**Answer: N**
questions.shortcut: Place J 2nd from top; N > L > M.

questions.q: 7 boys B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6 and B7 are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). B3 is not next to B7. B4 is next to both B1 and B7. B6 is second to the left of B7. B5 is second to the left of B6. Who is to the immediate left of B3?
questions.solution:
With B7 fixed, B6 (second to B7's left) and B5 (second to B6's left) take their seats; B4 must sit beside both B1 and B7, and B3 must avoid B7, which leaves B5 immediately to B3's left.

**Answer: B5**
questions.shortcut: Anchor B7 → B6 → B5; B4–B1 forced.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

BG12 : EJ59 :: PQ48 : ST95 :: LM33 : ?
questions.solution:
Letters jump +3 (B→E, G→J; P→S, Q→T) and numbers jump +47 (12→59, 48→95), so LM33 → OP80.

**Answer: OP80**

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AK40 : EE100 :: BM60 : ? :: DL80 : HF200
questions.solution:
Letters shift +4 and −6 (A→E, K→E; D→H, L→F) and numbers multiply by 2.5 (40→100, 80→200), so BM60 → FG150.

**Answer: FG150**

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the first number in the same way as the fourth number is related to the third number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

2436 : ? :: 777 : 257 :: 1812 : 602
questions.solution:
The second number is one-third of the first minus 2: 777/3 − 2 = 257 and 1812/3 − 2 = 602, so 2436/3 − 2 = 810.

**Answer: 810**

questions.q: In a certain coded language 'WEES' is coded as 'ZJCO' and 'EACH' is coded as 'HFAD'. How will 'PREY' be coded in the same code language?
questions.solution:
The shift pattern repeats by position: +3, +5, −2, −4 (WEES→ZJCO and EACH→HFAD both fit). PREY → S, W, C, U = SWCU.

**Answer: SWCU**

questions.q: A clock shows the correct time at 6 AM. The clock gains 2 seconds every 5 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 4 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
From 6 AM to 4 PM is 10 hours = 120 five-minute intervals, so the clock gains 120 × 2 = 240 seconds = 4 minutes and shows 4:04 PM.

**Answer: 4:04**
questions.shortcut: 2 s per 5 min → 4 min in 10 h.

questions.q: Father's age 15 years ago from present was 6 times of the age of his son 3 years ago from present. Son's age after 11 years from present is 16 years. What is the ratio of present ages of father and son?
questions.solution:
The son is now 16 − 11 = 5, so 3 years ago he was 2; the father 15 years ago was 6 × 2 = 12, i.e. 27 now, giving 27 : 5.

**Answer: 27 : 5**
